\section[la sentencia]{la sentencia — the court ruling, the judgment; the sentence}

\label{lesson:ES-C626-sentencia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to report, then the Spanish for the report.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la sentencia}
\textbf{la sentencia} — \textquotedblleft{}the court ruling, the judgment; the sentence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La sentencia sale mañana.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The ruling comes out tomorrow.}
\end{quote}

A court decision; \emph{dictar sentencia} — to pass judgment. A sentence in grammar is \emph{la oración} or \emph{la frase}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sentencia} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{sententia} 'way of thinking, opinion, verdict', built on \emph{sentire} 'to feel, to think' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la sentencia}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la sentencia}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la sentencia}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to report, then the Spanish for the report, then say \emph{la sentencia} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la sentencia mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The court ruling, the judgment; the sentence\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la acusación]{la acusación — the accusation, the charge}

\label{lesson:ES-C626-acusacion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the report, then the Spanish for the court ruling.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la acusación}
\textbf{la acusación} — \textquotedblleft{}the accusation, the charge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La acusación es muy grave.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The accusation is very serious.}
\end{quote}

In court \emph{la acusación} is also the prosecution.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{acusación} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{accusatio} 'an accusation', built on \emph{accusare}, from \emph{ad} and \emph{causa} 'case at law' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la acusación}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la acusación}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the report, then the Spanish for the court ruling, then say \emph{la acusación} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la acusación mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The accusation, the charge\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[el tribunal]{el tribunal — the court}

\label{lesson:ES-C626-tribunal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the court ruling, then the Spanish for the accusation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el tribunal}
\textbf{el tribunal} — \textquotedblleft{}the court\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El caso llegó al tribunal.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The case reached the court.}
\end{quote}

Also an exam board: \emph{el tribunal del examen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tribunal} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{tribunal}, the raised seat of the tribunes, built on \emph{tribunus} and \emph{tribus} 'tribe' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[culpable]{culpable — guilty; the culprit}

\label{lesson:ES-C626-culpable}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the accusation, then the Spanish for the court.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: culpable}
\textbf{culpable} — \textquotedblleft{}guilty; the culprit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El juez lo declaró culpable.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The judge found him guilty.}
\end{quote}

The opposite is \emph{inocente}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{culpable} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{culpabilis} 'blameworthy', built on \emph{culpa} 'fault' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the accusation, then the Spanish for the court, then say \emph{culpable} again

\section[el fraude]{el fraude — the fraud}

\label{lesson:ES-C626-fraude}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the court, then the Spanish for guilty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el fraude}
\textbf{el fraude} — \textquotedblleft{}the fraud\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Fue un fraude de millones de euros.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It was a fraud worth millions of euros.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Fraude fiscal} — tax fraud.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{fraude} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{fraus, fraudis} 'deceit, harm' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
